awd_titl_txt: I-Corps: Translation Potential of Advanced AI Solutions to Transform Education, Research, and Institutional Efficiency
awd_abstract_narration:
The broader impact/commercial potential of this I-Corps project is the development of an innovative initiative poised to transform the educational landscape through artificial intelligence. This technology aims to improve learning experiences by providing personalized, efficient, and accessible educational tools for students, educators, institutions, researchers, and publishers. By leveraging advanced artificial intelligence (AI), the proposed tool enhances operational efficiency, accelerates research innovation, and democratizes access to educational resources. Central to its mission is the mitigation of inequality among students, faculty, and researchers by removing prevalent barriers to accessing information and learning resources. This technology is particularly beneficial in improving retention rates among low-income and marginalized groups, who often face disproportionate challenges in educational settings. The commercial potential lies in its wide applicability across various educational settings, including K-12 schools, higher education institutions, professional training programs, and academic publishing. 

This I-Corps project utilizes experiential learning coupled with a first-hand investigation of the industry ecosystem to assess the translation potential of the technology. This solution is based on the development of intelligent agents designed to cater to the specific needs of users within the academic ecosystem. The artificial intelligence (AI) tools include emotionally aware assistants for students, automated grading systems for educators, and data-driven insights for institutional decision-making. The project builds on a decade of AI research, including advancements in adaptive learning systems, data analytics, and user experience design, integrating these advances into practical, user-focused solutions. The technology incorporates a robust Software-as-a-Service platform with a container architecture for efficient load balancing and resource allocation. It utilizes a dual approach for its AI models, incorporating Application Programming Interface (API) based models for advanced natural language tasks and open-source tools for textual and multimodal analysis. The tool showcases significant intellectual advantages, such as flexibility in model selection, fine-tuned domain-specific models, and comprehensive review capabilities. This approach promises to enhance educational outcomes and operational efficiencies, ultimately contributing to a more educated and technologically adept society.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
Scientific discovery, academic advancement, and innovation all depend on a critical process: peer review. Whether for publishing a research article or securing a grant, this system acts as the gatekeeper for new knowledge. However, this system is under immense strain. Researchers face long delays, reviewer fatigue is high, and the process can be inconsistent. For graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, and new faculty, these delays are more than just an inconvenience; they are a direct barrier to career progression and the dissemination of their research.

To address this challenge, our team participated in the National Science Foundation (NSF) I-Corps program. This program empowers scientists and engineers to explore the commercial potential of their research by talking directly to potential customers. Our initial idea was a broad hub for academic AI solutions, a suite of artificial intelligence tools to help with various academic tasks.

Major Goals and Accomplishments

The primary goal of our I-Corps project was not to build the technology, but to listen. We set out to test our assumptions by conducting over 100 interviews with the people who live in this system every day. Over seven weeks, our team conducted 111 interviews with PhD students, postdocs, tenured professors, journal editors, university administrators, and leaders at major publishing houses and funding agencies.

This customer discovery process was transformative and led us to two major pivots:

  1. Finding the Focus: We quickly learned that a broad "AI assistant" was too vague. The most severe and consistently-voiced pain point was the bottleneck of peer review. This led us to focus on a new, highly-specific product concept for an AI-powered reviewer, a tool designed to help researchers improve their manuscripts and proposals before they ever submit them.
  2. Finding the Customer: We initially assumed our customers would be large organizations like publishers or universities. Our interviews showed that such organizations are more risk averse to adopt new technology and have concerns about intellectual property.

Instead, we found a passionate and motivated customer base in the individual researchers themselves: Graduate Research Assistants (PhDs), Postdoctoral Researchers, and Tenure-Track Faculty. This "bottom-up" market feels the pain of rejection and delays most acutely. Their primary goal is to increase their chances of acceptance, and they are actively seeking tools to help them succeed.

Impact on Research, Education, and Society

The most significant outcome of this project is a validated pathway to market. This I-Corps grant successfully de-risked our technology and provided the evidence needed to make a "Go" decision for commercialization. Our team successfully secured follow-on Proof of Concept funding from the Iowa Economic Development Authority (IEDA) to build the first version of our product. Regarding its societal impact, by empowering individual researchers, ReviewerAI aims to level the playing field. It can serve as a virtual mentor, offering guidance to non-native English speakers or those at less-resourced institutions. Ultimately, by helping researchers improve their work and reduce review times, our goal is to accelerate the entire cycle of scientific discovery. Faster science leads to faster solutions—from new medical breakthroughs to innovations in engineering—benefiting all of society.
